_source: U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications API v4.0.1, service /api/rstt/oneday (docs https://aa.usno.navy.mil/data/api). Retrieved 2026-09-10 by curl from this repo's dev box. Every time below is a verbatim value from the response at the URL recorded beside it; nothing here is estimated, recalled or interpolated.
_gaps: The oneday service publishes CIVIL twilight only ('Begin/End Civil Twilight'), so nautical and astronomical twilight have NO reference value here and sun-moon.test.mjs covers those by internal consistency instead. 'fracillum' is USNO's whole-percent illuminated fraction, which is the fraction at 12:00 local time — the instant the engine is asked for when comparing. The service takes a fixed UTC offset, so a daylight-saving transition date needs one query per offset; the spring-forward case records both and says which value each grounds.
_springForward: The tz=-5 response (the offset in force in New York from 00:00 to 02:00 that day) lists no Rise: the rise the tz=-4 response puts at 00:03 is 04:03 UTC, which in America/New_York is 23:03 on 2026-03-07, still EST. The next rise, from the 2026-03-09 tz=-4 response at 01:03 (= 05:03 UTC), falls after this 23-hour local day ends at 04:00 UTC. So on the New York calendar day 2026-03-08 the Moon sets and never rises.

usnoSunPhenomena: Object continuously above the Twilight Limit
